description_full: Nayax Ltd., a fintech company, designs, develops, and sells integrated POS devices and software for automated self-service customers in-house in the United States, Europe, the United Kingdom, Australia, Israel, and internationally. It offers POS, cashless payments, and charging stations, such as VPOS Touch, Onyx, Nova Market, DOT, Nova C4, Nova C3, EV-Meter, EV Kiosk, Nova 55F, Nova 22, Nova 156, Nova Modu, and Nova Kiosk; management suite and telemetry solutions, Nayax Core Management Suite, MoMa, Vending Management System, Nayax Energy Core, and Retail Management Cloud; marketing, loyalty, and consumer engagement platforms, such as Monyx Wallet and Weezmo; and payments and integrations solutions, including API Suite and Coinbridge. The company serves vending machines, kiosks, self-checkouts, ticketing machines, laundromats, gaming terminals, and EV charging stations. Nayax Ltd. has a strategic alliance with Getnet Payments S.L. The company was incorporated in 2005 and is headquartered in Herzliya, Israel.

financial_summary: Nayax Ltd. is a small-cap technology business with a $1.9B market cap on $400M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +32% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +9.7pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -7% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 41%.

The business throws off $35M in free cash flow — roughly 9 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.13× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 2.7× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 57% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
